evidence.claim: An early tourist trail links the towns along Lake Michigan
evidence.quote: The West Michigan Pike is a historic trail leading beachgoers from all over the nation to unique and scenic towns along Lake Michigan shoreline.

evidence.claim: The West Michigan Pike connects New Buffalo and Ludington, following US 31 and business loops through lakeshore towns.
evidence.quote: it runs from New Buffalo on I-94 to Ludington, following US 31 except between business loops at South Haven, Muskegon, Whitehall–Montague and Pentwater.

evidence.claim: North of Holland, the highway runs inland from Lake Michigan through fields and forests.
evidence.quote: This section of US 31 runs through a mix of farm fields and forests as it runs to the community of Agnew.

evidence.claim: North of Holland, the highway runs inland from Lake Michigan through fields and forests.
evidence.quote: Northwest of Holland, the highway runs as a four-lane expressway and divided highway parallel, but inland from, the Lake Michigan shoreline.

evidence.claim: Michigan Beachtowns identifies historic, cultural, recreational and scenic values as the basis for its 2016 Pure Michigan Byway designation.
evidence.quote: The West Michigan Pike byway was added to the Michigan Department of Transportation’s collection of Pure Michigan Byways™ in 2016 based on its intrinsic historic, cultural, recreational, and scenic values.

evidence.claim: The Pike was developed as a tourist road for vacationers.
evidence.quote: Developed in 1911 as a pioneering tourist road, the West Michigan Pike was designed for vacationers seeking both relaxation and adventure.

evidence.claim: The West Michigan Lake Shore Highway Association formed in 1912 and reorganized as the West Michigan Pike Association in 1913.
evidence.quote: The West Michigan Lake Shore Highway Association was founded on January 10, 1912, and the group reorganized on May 30, 1913, as the West Michigan Pike Association.

evidence.claim: Its auto trail reached Mackinaw City, marked by concrete posts eight feet tall.
evidence.quote: Their auto trail was marked by a series of concrete markers eight feet (2.4 m) tall along the 400-mile-long (640 km) roadway from the Indiana state line northward to Mackinaw City.

evidence.claim: State highways in the corridor became US 31 in 1926.
evidence.quote: These state highways were redesignated US 31 on November 11, 1926, when the US Highway System was approved.

evidence.claim: Freeway construction began in the 1950s; residents later sought byway recognition for the former Pike.
evidence.quote: Later, sections were converted into freeways starting in the 1950s.

evidence.claim: Freeway construction began in the 1950s; residents later sought byway recognition for the former Pike.
evidence.quote: A group of area residents initiated an effort to have the former West Michigan Pike designated what is now called a Pure Michigan Byway.

evidence.claim: A Preserve America grant supported a historical survey from 2007 to 2010. The initial byway proposal extended to Mackinaw City, but the route approved in 2016 stopped at Ludington.
evidence.quote: A Preserve America grant funded a survey from June 2007 through September 2010

evidence.claim: A Preserve America grant supported a historical survey from 2007 to 2010. The initial byway proposal extended to Mackinaw City, but the route approved in 2016 stopped at Ludington.
evidence.quote: The initial proposals had the byway continuing to Mackinaw City, but as approved in 2016, it runs from New Buffalo on I-94 to Ludington

evidence.claim: From New Buffalo, the northbound journey leads to South Haven and Holland, then Grand Haven.
evidence.quote: it runs from New Buffalo on I-94 to Ludington

evidence.claim: From New Buffalo, the northbound journey leads to South Haven and Holland, then Grand Haven.
evidence.quote: I-196/US 31 continues north-northeasterly toward Holland.

evidence.claim: From New Buffalo, the northbound journey leads to South Haven and Holland, then Grand Haven.
evidence.quote: before continuing into the southern end of Grand Haven.

evidence.claim: In Grand Haven, US 31 becomes a boulevard before crossing the Grand River.
evidence.quote: In that city, the highway follows a four-lane boulevard with a grass median. On the northern edge of the city of Grand Haven, US 31 crosses the Grand River on a bascule bridge

evidence.claim: Beyond Muskegon, a business loop connects Whitehall and Montague.
evidence.quote: a business loop curves off to the west to connect the two communities with the freeway.

evidence.claim: Farther north, the highway passes Hart and crosses the Pentwater River before reaching Ludington.
evidence.quote: North of the trail crossing, US 31 has a business spur for Hart that runs east into that town; north of this interchange, the freeway crosses the Pentwater River near the community of Pentwater.

evidence.claim: Farther north, the highway passes Hart and crosses the Pentwater River before reaching Ludington.
evidence.quote: North of Pentwater, US 31 crosses into Mason County and passes Bass Lake and the Ludington Pumped Storage Power Plant

evidence.claim: Silver Lake’s dunes offer a separate excursion from the highway corridor.
evidence.quote: public recreation area bordering Lake Michigan and Silver Lake, four miles (6.4 km) west of Mears

evidence.claim: Holland’s tulips began with a teacher’s proposal. In 1927, biology teacher Lida Rogers suggested planting them to beautify the city and recognize its Dutch heritage.
evidence.quote: The festival originated after Holland High School biology teacher Lida Rogers proposed in 1927 that tulips be used as a civic beautification project and as a recognition of the city's Dutch heritage.

evidence.claim: The city bought 100,000 bulbs from the Netherlands the following year. Their 1929 bloom brought the first Tulip Time celebration.
evidence.quote: The city purchased 100,000 tulip bulbs from the Netherlands in 1928, and the first Tulip Time celebration was held when they bloomed in 1929.

evidence.claim: Holland hosts the festival each May.
evidence.quote: Holland hosts the annual Tulip Time Festival in May.

evidence.claim: Another imported landmark arrived in 1964: De Zwaan, the Dutch windmill at Windmill Island Gardens. The island opened to the public the following year.
evidence.quote: Windmill Island Gardens contains De Zwaan, a Dutch windmill that was relocated from the Netherlands to Holland in 1964; Windmill Island opened to the public the following year.

evidence.claim: The festival’s present program includes tulip displays, parades and Dutch cultural performances, continuing the connection between planting and public celebration.
evidence.quote: Festival activities include tulip displays, parades and Dutch cultural performances.

evidence.claim: Two red lights and a catwalk mark Grand Haven’s waterfront.
evidence.quote: The current lighthouses, painted red, were built in 1875 (outer light) and 1905 (inner). They are connected by a lighted catwalk, which runs along the pier to the shore.

evidence.claim: The city stands at the mouth of the Grand River on Lake Michigan.
evidence.quote: Grand Haven is located on the eastern shore of Lake Michigan at the mouth of the Grand River

evidence.claim: During the nineteenth century it developed as a lumber, shipping and shipbuilding center.
evidence.quote: In the mid-to-late 19th century, Grand Haven developed as a logging, lumber mill, and shipping town, as well as a shipbuilding center.

evidence.claim: Lights were first built on the south pier in 1839 to mark the navigable channel.
evidence.quote: Given the importance of shipping and water trade to the city, the Grand Haven Lighthouses were built in 1839 on the south pier to mark the most navigable channel into the river.

evidence.claim: The present outer and inner lights date to 1875 and 1905. Their connecting catwalk extends along the pier to shore.
evidence.quote: The current lighthouses, painted red, were built in 1875 (outer light) and 1905 (inner). They are connected by a lighted catwalk, which runs along the pier to the shore.

evidence.claim: The railroad’s waterfront depot and offices have also found a new role, adapted for use as a historical museum.
evidence.quote: The city was served by the Grand Trunk Railway, which ran along the waterfront near the river. Its depot and offices have been adapted for use as a historical museum.

evidence.claim: Silver Lake State Park borders both Silver Lake and Lake Michigan, combining mature forest with more than 2,000 acres of dunes.
evidence.quote: Silver Lake State Park is a 2,936-acre (1,188 ha) public recreation area bordering Lake Michigan and Silver Lake, four miles (6.4 km) west of Mears in Oceana County, Michigan. The state park is composed of mature forest land and over 2,000 acres (810 ha) of sand dunes.

evidence.claim: The park began with Carrie E. Mears’s 1920 donation of 25 acres on Silver Lake’s east side.
evidence.quote: The park originated in 1920 when 25 acres on the east side of Silver Lake were donated for park purposes by Carrie E. Mears

evidence.claim: A federal transfer of 900 acres followed in 1926. That land became Sand Dunes State Park; the two parks merged under a 1949 plan, with new boundaries dedicated in 1951.
evidence.quote: In 1926, the federal government transferred 900 acres to the state, which became Sand Dunes State Park in 1949. Based upon a 1949 master plan, the two were merged, with Silver Lake State Park seeing its new boundaries dedicated in 1951.

evidence.claim: The northern dunes allow private motorized vehicles; the middle section is reserved for walking.
evidence.quote: The northern area is an all-terrain vehicle dunes area where private motorized vehicle may be driven, the middle of the park is a non-vehicle area (the Walking Dunes)

evidence.claim: The park also encompasses Silver Lake’s entire western shoreline.
evidence.quote: The park encompasses the entire 1.6-mile (2.6 km) western shoreline of Silver Lake

flags: Dropped 184 miles, Michigan’s first paved road built for visitors, and credit for starting the tourist trade: the MDOT cache is only an archive wrapper and the other pages do not establish those claims.
